events.title: All India Muslim League founded
events.summary: Muslim landlords and nawabs form the All India Muslim League at Dacca (December 1906); it supports partition and asks for separate electorates (NCERT).
events.detail: In October 1906 a deputation of Muslim leaders led by the Aga Khan met Viceroy Minto at Simla and asked for separate electorates. In December 1906 a group of Muslim landlords and nawabs formed the All India Muslim League at Dacca (NCERT). It supported the partition of Bengal and desired separate electorates — a demand conceded in 1909 (NCERT).
causes: Fear among Muslim elites of Hindu-dominated politics.
Support for the partition of Bengal (NCERT).
The British encouraged it to weaken the Congress.
course: 1 October 1906: Simla Deputation to Lord Minto.
30 December 1906: League founded at Dacca (NCERT).
outcomes: Separate electorates were conceded in 1909 (NCERT).
The League later demanded Pakistan (1940).
facts: The All India Muslim League was formed at Dacca in 1906 (NCERT).
It desired separate electorates, conceded in 1909 (NCERT).

participants.role: Led the Simla Deputation and became the League's first president.
Nawab of Dacca who hosted the founding.
Viceroy who received the Simla Deputation.

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Calcutta Congress: Swaraj declared the goal
events.summary: Under Dadabhai Naoroji the Calcutta session (1906) declares Swaraj the goal and backs Swadeshi, boycott and national education.
events.detail: To avoid a split between Moderates and Radicals, the old leader Dadabhai Naoroji was made president. For the first time the Congress spoke of "Swaraj" as its aim and passed resolutions on Swadeshi, boycott and national education.
causes: The Swadeshi movement after the partition of Bengal.
Rising Radical influence.
outcomes: The split was only postponed — it came at Surat (1907).

participants.role: Presided and declared Swaraj the goal.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Vandemataram movement in Andhra
events.summary: Bipin Chandra Pal's tour (April 1907) sets coastal Andhra alight with Swadeshi; Chilakamarthi's poem becomes its song.
events.detail:
Bipin Chandra Pal spoke at Vijayawada, Machilipatnam, Kakinada and Rajahmundry in April 1907. At Rajahmundry, Chilakamarthi Lakshmi Narasimham recited his poem "Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu" — India is a fine milch cow, milked by the British. Students wore Vandemataram badges; some were expelled.

Clashes at Kakinada (1907) and later at Kotappakonda (1909) led to arrests and harsh sentences.
causes: Anger at the partition of Bengal.
Pal's Swadeshi message.
course: April 1907: Pal tours Andhra; huge meetings.
Rajahmundry students expelled for wearing Vandemataram badges.
May 1907: riots at Kakinada after a British officer assaults a youth.
1909: Kotappakonda riots (Guntur).
outcomes: Swadeshi stores, national schools (Andhra Jateeya Kalasala, Machilipatnam, 1910) and Telugu nationalist papers grew.
Fed into the Andhra movement for a separate province.

alsoOn.text: Andhra Jateeya Kalasala (national college) founded at Machilipatnam.

events.yearHook: April 1907: two years after the Bengal partition (1905); Surat split later that year.

participants.role: His speeches started the movement in Andhra.
His poem became the anthem of the movement.

events.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)
events.before: The partition of **Bengal** (1905) set off Swadeshi; Telugu students and lawyers read about it in papers like **Krishna Patrika** (1902).
events.after: National schools (**Andhra Jateeya Kalasala**, Machilipatnam, 1910) and the demand for an Andhra province (**Bapatla**, 1913) followed. **Home Rule** leagues of Annie Besant spread in Andhra towns in 1916–17.
events.today: Chilakamarthi's "Bharata khandambu chakkani padi aavu" is taught in Telugu schools.
events.mnemonic: Vandemataram events in Andhra by date "P-K-K-T": Pal's tour (Apr 1907), Kakinada riot (Jul 1907), Kotappakonda (Feb 1909), Tenali bomb (Apr 1909).

examAngle.point: The Kakinada riot case (July 1907) was the first criminal case of the Vandemataram movement in Andhra; Pal's tour was April 1907, Kotappakonda riots February 1909, Tenali bomb case April 1909.
examAngle.context: At Kakinada a British doctor (Kemp) assaulted a student wearing a Vandemataram badge; the town rioted. It shows how a badge became a crime.

events.title: Muzaffarpur bomb; Khudiram Bose hanged; Tilak jailed
events.summary: Revolutionaries throw a bomb at Muzaffarpur; Khudiram Bose is hanged and Tilak is sentenced to six years in Mandalay for defending them.
events.detail: Some individuals now suggested that revolutionary violence would be necessary to overthrow British rule (NCERT). In April 1908 Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage at Muzaffarpur they thought carried the judge Kingsford; two Englishwomen were killed. Khudiram was hanged. The Alipore Bomb Case followed against Aurobindo Ghosh and others. Tilak was sentenced to six years in Mandalay for articles in Kesari.
causes: Repression of the Swadeshi movement.
outcomes: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act (1908) and Explosive Substances Act.
events.yearHook: 1908: Tilak to Mandalay — he came back in 1914.

participants.role: Tried in the Alipore Bomb Case; acquitted.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Morley–Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)
events.summary: Councils are enlarged and separate electorates for Muslims are introduced (NCERT).
events.detail: The Act increased the elected members of the legislative councils and let them discuss the budget. Some seats were reserved for Muslims, to be elected only by Muslim voters (NCERT). This tempted politicians to gather a following by distributing favours to their own religious groups (NCERT). S.P. Sinha became the first Indian on the Viceroy's Executive Council.
causes: To win over the Moderates after the Surat split.
The Muslim League's demand for separate electorates (NCERT).
outcomes: Separate electorates divided Indian politics along religious lines (NCERT).
Satyendra Prasanna Sinha became the first Indian member of the Executive Council.
facts: The demand for separate electorates was conceded by the government in 1909 (NCERT).

pairs.left: First Indian on Viceroy's Executive Council

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Delhi Durbar: partition annulled, capital moved to Delhi
events.summary: At the Delhi Durbar (12 December 1911) King George V announces the end of Bengal's partition and the shift of the capital from Calcutta to Delhi.
events.detail: The Swadeshi agitation had made the partition unworkable. Bengal was reunited; Bihar and Orissa and Assam became separate provinces. New Delhi, designed by Lutyens, was inaugurated in 1931.
causes: The Swadeshi movement made the partition unworkable.
outcomes: Bengal reunited; Bihar–Orissa and Assam made separate provinces.
Delhi became the capital.
facts: Partition of Bengal annulled in 1911.
Jana Gana Mana was first sung at the Calcutta Congress of December 1911.

alsoOn.text: A bomb is thrown at Viceroy Hardinge as he enters Delhi (Delhi Conspiracy Case).

participants.role: Viceroy who carried out the changes.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Ghadar Party
events.summary: Indian immigrants on the Pacific coast of North America form the Ghadar Party under Lala Har Dayal to overthrow British rule by armed revolt.
events.detail: Indian workers in the USA and Canada faced racism. In 1913 they formed the Hindustan Ghadar Party at San Francisco and printed the paper Ghadar. In 1914–15 many returned to India to start a revolt in the army; it was crushed (Lahore Conspiracy Case). The Komagata Maru ship (1914), carrying would-be emigrants refused entry by Canada, was fired on at Budge Budge.
causes: Racism against Indians in North America.
Revolutionary nationalism.
outcomes: A planned army revolt in February 1915 failed; many were hanged.

alsoOn.text: The Komagata Maru returns from Canada; police fire on passengers at Budge Budge.

events.yearHook: Ghadar 1913, Komagata Maru 1914 — just before the war.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
facts: Also spelt Ghadr.

Revolutionary papers abroad: Indian Sociologist — Shyamji Krishna Varma (London); Islamic Fraternity — Muhammad Barkatullah (Tokyo); The Talwar — Virendra Chattopadhyay (Berlin); Swadesh Sevak — G.D. Kumar (Vancouver) (APPSC Group-1 key).

events.title: Gandhi returns from South Africa
events.summary: Gandhiji, aged 46, arrives in India on 9 January 1915 and spends a year travelling to understand the country (NCERT).
events.detail: In South Africa Gandhi had led non-violent marches against racist restrictions and was already known internationally (NCERT). In 1895 he had helped found the Natal Congress (NCERT). Back in India, on Gokhale's advice, he spent his first year travelling through the country (NCERT) and set up an ashram at Sabarmati.
causes: His work in South Africa (1893–1914) was done.
outcomes: His first local struggles — Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad — followed in 1917–18 (NCERT).
facts: Gandhiji arrived in India in 1915 from South Africa, aged 46 (NCERT).
9 January is celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
The Congress Moderates and Radicals reunite in December 1915 (NCERT).

participants.role: His political guru; advised him to see India first.

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: August Declaration (Montagu)
events.summary: On 20 August 1917 Montagu announces "the progressive realisation of responsible government in India" as British policy.
events.detail: To win Indian support in the war, the Secretary of State promised more Indians in the administration and gradual self-government. It led to the Montagu–Chelmsford Report (1918) and the Act of 1919.
causes: The need for Indian support in the First World War.
The Home Rule agitation.
outcomes: Led to the Government of India Act 1919.
events.yearHook: 1917: Champaran, the Russian Revolution and the August Declaration.

participants.role: Viceroy who worked with him on the reforms.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Kheda satyagraha and the Ahmedabad mill strike
events.summary: Gandhi leads Kheda peasants against land revenue and Ahmedabad millworkers in a successful strike (NCERT).
events.detail: In Kheda, Gujarat, crops had failed but the government demanded full revenue. Gandhi, with Vallabhbhai Patel, led a no-revenue campaign. In Ahmedabad he led a successful millworkers' strike in 1918 (NCERT), fasting for the first time in India to press the mill-owners.
causes: Crop failure and full revenue demand in Kheda.
Wage dispute in the Ahmedabad mills.
outcomes: Revenue was suspended for the poorest; millworkers got a 35% raise.
Gandhi and Patel became partners.
facts: In Ahmedabad, Gandhi led a successful millworkers' strike in 1918 (NCERT).
Gandhi came into contact with Rajendra Prasad and Vallabhbhai Patel in these local movements (NCERT).
events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms)
events.summary: Introduces dyarchy in the provinces and a two-house central legislature.
events.detail: Provincial subjects were split: "transferred" subjects (education, health, local government) went to Indian ministers answerable to the legislature, while "reserved" subjects (police, finance, land revenue) stayed with the Governor. At the centre a bicameral legislature was created. Separate electorates were extended to Sikhs, Indian Christians and others.
causes: The August Declaration (1917).
Indian demands for self-government after the war.
course: Dyarchy in the provinces: transferred and reserved subjects.
Bicameral central legislature (Legislative Assembly and Council of State).
A statutory commission to review it after ten years.
outcomes: The Congress rejected it as inadequate; dyarchy failed.
Led to the Simon Commission (1927–28).
facts: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces by the Act of 1919.
events.yearHook: Acts 1909, 1919, 1935 — reforms about every ten to sixteen years.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Chirala-Perala movement
events.summary: The people of Chirala and Perala leave their town and live in a camp rather than pay a heavy new municipal tax.
events.detail: In 1919 Chirala-Perala was made a municipality with high taxes. Led by Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, people refused to pay. In 1921, on Gandhi's suggestion of non-cooperation, about 15,000 people left the town and lived for eleven months in a new settlement, Ramnagar. Many leaders were jailed.
causes: A new municipality with heavy taxes on a poor town.
outcomes: The people returned after a long struggle; the movement became a model of Gandhian protest in Andhra.
events.yearHook: 1919: same year as Jallianwala Bagh. The town leaves in 1921 and lives in Ramnagar for 11 months.
events.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)
facts: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya raised a volunteer corps called the "Ramadandu" (APPSC Group-II 2018 key).
events.before: The government made Chirala-Perala a municipality and raised the tax sharply.
events.after: The people came back after many arrests; Gopalakrishnayya ("**Andhra Ratna**") was jailed. The protest became a model of Gandhian non-payment in Andhra.
events.today: Chirala is in Bapatla district; it is a centre for handloom weaving.

events.title: Moplah (Malabar) rebellion
events.summary: Muslim tenants (Moplahs) of Malabar rise against landlords and the British during the Khilafat movement.
events.detail: The rising began as anti-British and anti-landlord but turned communal in places. It was crushed by the army; in the "Wagon tragedy" over 60 prisoners suffocated in a closed railway wagon.
causes: Tenancy grievances against landlords.
The Khilafat agitation.
outcomes: Crushed by martial law; it damaged Hindu–Muslim unity.
events.yearHook: 1921: Moplahs in Malabar, forest satyagraha in Palnadu.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Non-Cooperation in Andhra: Pedanandipadu and Palnadu
events.summary: Guntur peasants refuse taxes at Pedanandipadu and stage forest satyagrahas in Palnadu (NCERT mentions the Guntur forest satyagrahas).
events.detail: In coastal Andhra liquor shops were picketed, and in Guntur district tribals and poor peasants staged a number of "forest satyagrahas", sending their cattle into forests without paying grazing fees (NCERT). At Pedanandipadu villagers refused land tax and village officers resigned. In Palnadu, Kanneganti Hanumanthu was shot dead by police (1922).
causes: Grazing fees and forest restrictions (NCERT).
Gandhi's call for non-cooperation.
outcomes: Suspended when Gandhi called off the movement (1922).
facts: In the Guntur district, tribals and poor peasants staged a number of forest satyagrahas (NCERT).
Leaders: Duggirala Gopala Krishnayya (Chirala–Perala), Kasinadhuni Nageswara Rao; Bhimavaram was a centre of the movement.
Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary, leader of the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign, was called "Andhra Sivaji" (APPSC Group-II 2018 key).
Kanneganti Hanumanthu led the "No Pullari (grass tax)" movement in Palnadu; Duggirala Gopala Krishnaiah led Chirala-Perala (APPSC Group-II 2025 key).
events.yearHook: Andhra's non-cooperation peaked in 1921, just like the all-India movement.

participants.role: Led the Palnadu forest satyagraha; shot in 1922.

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"; Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)
events.before: Gandhi visited Andhra; the AICC met at **Bezawada** (March–April 1921) and set targets: one crore members, one crore rupees (Tilak Swaraj Fund), 20 lakh charkhas.
events.after: After Chauri Chaura (1922) the movement stopped; Andhra leaders hosted the **Kakinada session** (1923). **Alluri** turned to armed revolt in the hills (1922).
events.today: Kanneganti Hanumanthu is remembered in Palnadu as a martyr of the grass-tax (pullari) fight.
events.mnemonic: Andhra non-cooperation "C-P-P": Chirala-Perala (town left), Pedanandipadu (no tax), Palnadu (forests and grass tax).

events.title: Chauri Chaura; Non-Cooperation called off
events.summary: On 4 February 1922 a crowd burns the police station at Chauri Chaura; Gandhi calls off the movement (NCERT).
events.detail: Gandhi was against violent movements. He abruptly called off the Non-Cooperation Movement when a crowd of peasants set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura; twenty-two policemen were killed. The peasants had been provoked by police firing on a peaceful demonstration (NCERT).
causes: Police firing on a peaceful demonstration (NCERT).
outcomes: Non-Cooperation ended (NCERT).
Many leaders were unhappy; some turned to the Swaraj Party, others to revolutionary methods.
facts: Twenty-two policemen were killed at Chauri Chaura (NCERT).
February 1922 (NCERT).

participants.role: Called off the movement; arrested in March 1922 and sentenced to six years.

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Swaraj Party
events.summary: C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru form the Swaraj Party to enter the councils and oppose the government from within (NCERT).
events.detail: After Non-Cooperation, Gandhians stressed constructive work in villages; C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru argued for fighting elections and entering the councils (NCERT). The Swarajists won many seats in 1923.
causes: Disagreement over the next step after Non-Cooperation (NCERT).
outcomes: Swarajists exposed the weakness of the 1919 reforms in the legislatures.
Gandhians built village support through constructive work (NCERT).
events.yearHook: Swaraj Party 1923 — founded at Gaya's aftermath; Kakinada Congress the same year.

participants.role: Mohammad Ali presided over the Kakinada Congress (1923).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Kakori train action
events.summary: HRA revolutionaries rob a train carrying government money at Kakori near Lucknow (9 August 1925).
events.detail: The Hindustan Republican Association needed money for arms. Its members stopped a train and took the government treasury. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, Rajendra Lahiri and Roshan Singh were hanged in 1927.
causes: Revolutionaries needed funds for arms.
outcomes: Four were hanged; the HRA was reorganised as the HSRA (1928).
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: RSS, the Communist Party and the Self Respect Movement
events.summary: Two important developments of the mid-1920s were the formation of the RSS and the Communist Party of India (NCERT); Periyar starts the Self Respect Movement.
events.detail: The RSS, a Hindu organisation, was founded at Nagpur by K.B. Hedgewar; the Communist Party of India held its first conference at Kanpur. These parties held very different ideas about the kind of country India should be (NCERT). In the south, Periyar founded the Self Respect Movement for the dignity of the lower castes (NCERT).
causes: Different responses to colonial rule and to caste.
outcomes: New political currents beside the Congress.
facts: The RSS and the Communist Party of India were formed in the mid-1920s (NCERT).
events.yearHook: 1925: RSS, CPI (Kanpur) and Self Respect — and Sarojini Naidu presides at Kanpur.
events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"; NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7 "Women, Caste and Reform"

events.title: Andhra University founded
events.summary: Andhra University is set up (first at Bezawada, then Waltair) — a long demand of the Andhra movement.
events.detail: The Andhra movement had demanded a university for Telugu speakers. Andhra University was established in 1926 with C.R. Reddy as its first Vice-Chancellor and moved to Waltair (Visakhapatnam).
causes: Demand of the Andhra Mahasabha for higher education in Andhra.
outcomes: A centre of Telugu learning and of the Andhra movement.
events.yearHook: Andhra University 1926 — thirteen years after the first Andhra Mahasabha (1913).
events.source: Andhra history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)
events.before: The **Andhra Mahasabha** (1913–) wanted a university for Telugu areas; Madras University served the whole south.
events.after: It moved to **Waltair** (Visakhapatnam). The choice of a coastal site worried Rayalaseema and was one cause of the **Sri Bagh Pact** (1937); **Sri Venkateswara University** (Tirupati, 1954) followed.
events.today: Andhra University (Visakhapatnam) is one of India's older state universities.

events.title: Ambedkar's Mahad satyagraha and temple entry
events.summary: In 1927 Ambedkar starts a temple entry movement; Dalits use water from the tank at Mahad (NCERT).
events.detail: In 1927 Ambedkar said: "We now want to go to the Tank only to prove that like others, we are also human beings" (NCERT). Brahman priests were outraged when Dalits used water from the temple tank (NCERT). Ambedkar led three temple-entry movements between 1927 and 1935 to make everyone see the power of caste prejudice (NCERT).
causes: Dalits were denied water from public tanks and entry into temples (NCERT).
outcomes: Made caste prejudice a national issue (NCERT).
The Kalaram temple entry movement at Nashik followed (1930).
facts: In 1927 Ambedkar started a temple entry movement (NCERT).
He led three such movements between 1927 and 1935 (NCERT).
events.yearHook: 1927: Mahad, and the Simon Commission is announced.
events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 7 "Women, Caste and Reform"

events.title: Nehru Report
events.summary: An all-parties committee under Motilal Nehru drafts a constitution for India based on Dominion Status.
events.detail: Answering the British challenge that Indians could not agree on a constitution, the report proposed Dominion Status, joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, and fundamental rights. The League rejected it; Jinnah put forward his Fourteen Points (1929).
causes: The all-white Simon Commission (NCERT).
Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to agree on a constitution.
outcomes: Split between those wanting Dominion Status and complete independence; led to the Purna Swaraj resolution (1929).

alsoOn.text: Jinnah puts forward his Fourteen Points.

participants.role: Rejected it and issued his Fourteen Points (1929).
Younger leaders like him wanted complete independence, not Dominion Status.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: HSRA and the killing of Saunders
events.summary: Bhagat Singh, Azad and others found the HSRA (1928); on 17 December 1928 they kill the police officer Saunders (NCERT).
events.detail: Revolutionary nationalists such as Bhagat Singh, Chandra Shekhar Azad and Sukhdev wanted a revolution of workers and peasants. They founded the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association in 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi (NCERT). On 17 December 1928 Bhagat Singh, Azad and Rajguru assassinated Saunders, a police officer involved in the lathi-charge that had caused the death of Lala Lajpat Rai (NCERT).
causes: The death of Lala Lajpat Rai after the police lathi-charge (NCERT).
outcomes: The Assembly bomb (1929) and the Lahore Conspiracy Case followed.
facts: HSRA: founded 1928 at Ferozeshah Kotla, Delhi (NCERT).
Saunders was killed on 17 December 1928 (NCERT).

The Hindustan Republican Association (1924, Kanpur) was founded by Sachindra Nath Sanyal, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee and Ram Prasad Bismil (APPSC Group-1 key); in 1928 Bhagat Singh and Chandra Shekhar Azad renamed it the HSRA.

participants.role: Founded the HSRA and took part in the action (NCERT).
Rajguru took part in the action; Sukhdev was a founder (NCERT).
His death after the lathi-charge was avenged (NCERT).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly
events.summary: On 8 April 1929 Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt throw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly "to make the deaf hear" (NCERT).
events.detail: The aim, as their leaflet explained, was not to kill but "to make the deaf hear" and to remind the foreign government of its callous exploitation (NCERT). They courted arrest shouting "Inquilab Zindabad".
causes: Protest against the Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill.
outcomes: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed on 23 March 1931 (NCERT).
facts: 8 April 1929: bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly (NCERT).
Bhagat Singh was executed on 23 March 1931 at age 23 (NCERT).

alsoOn.text: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru are executed on 23 March 1931 (NCERT).

participants.role: Threw the bomb with B.K. Dutt (NCERT).
Executed with Bhagat Singh on 23 March 1931 (NCERT).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Chittagong Armoury Raid
events.summary: Surya Sen's Indian Republican Army raids the armoury at Chittagong (18 April 1930).
events.detail: About 65 young revolutionaries seized the police and auxiliary armouries and fought British troops at Jalalabad hill. Many were killed; Surya Sen was caught in 1933 and hanged in 1934. Women such as Pritilata Waddedar and Kalpana Dutt took part.
causes: Revolutionary nationalism in Bengal.
outcomes: Severe repression in Chittagong; inspired young revolutionaries.
events.yearHook: April 1930 — the same month Gandhi reached Dandi.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: First Round Table Conference
events.summary: The British hold a conference in London (November 1930–January 1931) on India's constitution; the Congress stays away.
events.detail: Princes, the Muslim League, the Hindu Mahasabha, liberals and Ambedkar for the depressed classes attended. Without the Congress, little could be decided.
causes: The Simon Commission report and Indian demands.
outcomes: Showed that no settlement was possible without the Congress → Gandhi–Irwin Pact.

alsoOn.text: Third Round Table Conference in London (November–December); the Congress does not attend.

events.yearHook: RTCs: 1930, 1931, 1932 — Gandhi only at the second.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Karachi Congress: Fundamental Rights resolution
events.summary: The Karachi session (March 1931), under Vallabhbhai Patel, endorses the Gandhi–Irwin Pact and passes resolutions on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy.
events.detail: Held days after Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were executed, the session was tense. It defined what Swaraj would mean for ordinary people: civil liberties, equality, minimum wages, free primary education and state control of key industries.
causes: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact needed approval.
outcomes: A forerunner of the Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of the Constitution.
facts: Patel served as President of the Congress in 1931 (NCERT).

participants.role: Presided over the session (NCERT: Congress president in 1931).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Second Round Table Conference
events.summary: Gandhi attends as the sole Congress representative (September–December 1931); the talks fail over minority representation.
events.detail: Gandhi claimed the Congress spoke for all Indians. The Muslim League, princes and Ambedkar demanded separate electorates; Gandhi opposed separate electorates for the depressed classes. He returned empty-handed and Civil Disobedience resumed in January 1932.
causes: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact (1931).
outcomes: Failed; Civil Disobedience resumed (1932–34).
Led to the Communal Award (1932).

participants.role: Demanded separate electorates for the depressed classes.
Viceroy; arrested Gandhi on his return.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Congress Socialist Party
events.summary: Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev and others form a socialist group inside the Congress.
events.detail: Socialists wanted the Congress to take up the cause of peasants and workers more strongly. Nehru and Bose sympathised with them.
causes: The Depression and peasant distress.
Influence of socialist ideas.
outcomes: Pushed the Congress towards land reform and labour rights.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
facts: N. G. Ranga was the pioneer of the Kisan (peasant) movement in Andhra — Ryots' Association, Indian Peasants' Institute at Nidubrolu (1933), and a founder of the All India Kisan Sabha (1936) (APPSC Group-II Screening 2018 key).

events.title: Provincial elections and Congress ministries
events.summary: Under the 1935 Act, elections are held in 1937; the Congress forms governments in 7 of 11 provinces (NCERT).
events.detail:
The combined struggles of the Indian people bore fruit when the 1935 Act prescribed provincial autonomy and the government announced elections in 1937 (NCERT). The Congress formed ministries in Madras, Bombay, the Central Provinces, the United Provinces, Bihar, Orissa and the NWFP (later also Assam). C. Rajagopalachari became Premier of Madras.

The provincial elections of 1937 seemed to convince the League that Muslims were a minority who would always play second fiddle; the Congress's refusal of a joint government in the United Provinces annoyed the League (NCERT).
causes: The Government of India Act 1935 (NCERT).
outcomes: Congress ministries ruled until October 1939 (NCERT).
The League grew hostile to the Congress (NCERT).
facts: The Congress formed governments in 7 out of 11 provinces in 1937 (NCERT).

participants.role: Became Premier of the Madras Presidency.
His League did poorly and turned towards a separate-nation idea (NCERT).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Haripura, Tripuri and the Forward Bloc
events.summary: Subhas Bose wins re-election at Tripuri (1939) against Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya, then resigns and forms the Forward Bloc.
events.detail: Bose was elected president at Haripura (1938). In 1939 he stood again and defeated Pattabhi Sitaramayya; Gandhi said the defeat was "more mine than his". The Working Committee would not cooperate, so Bose resigned and founded the Forward Bloc.
causes: Bose wanted a fight with the British; Gandhi and the Working Committee did not.
outcomes: Bose left the Congress leadership; the Forward Bloc was formed (May 1939).

alsoOn.text: Subhas Chandra Bose presides over the Haripura Congress.

participants.role: Won at Tripuri, resigned, and formed the Forward Bloc.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Lahore Resolution of the Muslim League
events.summary: On 23 March 1940 the League demands "Independent States" for Muslims in the north-west and east; it does not mention partition or Pakistan (NCERT).
events.detail: From the late 1930s the League began viewing Muslims as a separate "nation" from Hindus (NCERT). At its Lahore session the League moved a resolution demanding "Independent States" for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas. The resolution did not mention partition or Pakistan (NCERT).
causes: The League felt Muslims would always be a minority in a democratic India after the 1937 elections (NCERT).
Congress refused a joint government in the United Provinces (1937) (NCERT).
outcomes: Became the basis of the demand for Pakistan (NCERT).
facts: The 1940 resolution did not mention partition or Pakistan (NCERT).
events.yearHook: Lahore 1929 Purna Swaraj; Lahore 1940 League resolution.

participants.role: Presided over the League session at Lahore.

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: August Offer and individual satyagraha
events.summary: Linlithgow offers Dominion Status "in the future" (August 1940); Gandhi starts limited individual satyagraha, with Vinoba Bhave as the first satyagrahi.
events.detail: The offer promised a body to frame a constitution after the war and assured minorities that no constitution would be imposed without their consent. The Congress rejected it. Gandhi chose individual satyagrahis to speak against the war: Vinoba Bhave (October 1940) first, Nehru second.
causes: The Congress demand for independence in return for war support (NCERT).
outcomes: Rejected; about 25,000 satyagrahis were jailed by 1941.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Cripps Mission
events.summary: Stafford Cripps offers Dominion Status after the war and a constituent assembly; the Congress and the League reject it (March–April 1942).
events.detail: Japan had reached Burma. The proposals let any province stay out of the new union — which seemed to open the door to partition — and gave no real power now. Gandhi is said to have called it "a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank".
causes: Japanese advance to India's borders.
Allied pressure on Britain for Indian support.
course: Dominion Status after the war.
An elected constituent assembly after the war.
Provinces free to stay out of the union.
Defence to remain under British control during the war.
outcomes: Rejected by all; led straight to Quit India.

participants.role: Rejected them for not conceding Pakistan.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
facts: Order: Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922) → Gandhi-Irwin Pact (Mar 1931) → Poona Pact (Sep 1932) → Cripps Mission (Mar 1942) (APPSC Group-II 2023 key).

events.title: Bengal famine
events.summary: A man-made famine kills about three million people in Bengal (1943).
events.detail: War-time hoarding, the loss of rice imports from Burma, a cyclone, and the government's priority to feed the army and cities caused prices to soar. Relief came late.
causes: Loss of Burmese rice after the Japanese conquest.
Hoarding and war-time demand.
Slow government relief.
outcomes: Deepened hatred of British rule.

participants.role: Viceroy who organised army relief from October 1943.

events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: C.R. Formula and the Gandhi–Jinnah talks
events.summary: Rajaji proposes a plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas after the war; Gandhi and Jinnah talk in Bombay (September 1944) but fail (NCERT shows both).
events.detail: The formula offered a separate state if the people of contiguous Muslim-majority districts voted for it after the war, with defence and communications shared. Jinnah wanted the whole of Punjab and Bengal and full sovereignty.
causes: The Pakistan demand after 1940.
outcomes: No agreement; the League's claim grew stronger.
events.yearHook: 1944: C.R. Formula and the INA at Imphal.

participants.role: Proposed the formula (NCERT shows him before the talks).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Wavell Plan and the Simla Conference
events.summary: Wavell proposes an all-Indian Executive Council; the Simla Conference (June–July 1945) fails because the League claims the sole right to name Muslim members (NCERT).
events.detail: At the end of the war the British opened negotiations. The talks failed because the League saw itself as the sole spokesperson of India's Muslims; the Congress could not accept this since many Muslims still supported it (NCERT).
causes: End of the war in Europe; release of Congress leaders.
outcomes: Failed; elections were ordered for 1945–46.

participants.role: Led the Congress delegation as its president.
Insisted the League alone would name Muslims (NCERT).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: INA trials at the Red Fort
events.summary: The trial of INA officers at the Red Fort (November 1945) brings protests across India (NCERT).
events.detail: Shah Nawaz Khan, Prem Sahgal and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon — a Muslim, a Hindu and a Sikh — were tried together. The Congress defence team included Bhulabhai Desai and Nehru. People across the country, from all walks of life, joined the protests (NCERT). Their sentences were remitted.
causes: The British prosecuted INA officers for "waging war against the King".
outcomes: Sentences remitted; British confidence in the army shaken.
facts: INA members were imprisoned and tried; people across India protested (NCERT).

participants.role: Leader of the INA whose officers were tried.

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Direct Action Day
events.summary: The League calls 16 August 1946 "Direct Action Day"; riots break out in Calcutta, killing thousands (NCERT).
events.detail: After the failure of the Cabinet Mission, the League decided on mass agitation for Pakistan. On 16 August riots broke out in Calcutta, lasting several days and killing thousands. By March 1947 violence had spread across northern India (NCERT).
causes: Failure of the Cabinet Mission plan (NCERT).
outcomes: Partition now became more or less inevitable (NCERT).
Riots spread to Noakhali, Bihar and Punjab.
facts: 16 August 1946 was Direct Action Day (NCERT).
events.yearHook: 16 August 1946 — one year before independence, almost to the day.

participants.role: Toured Noakhali and Bihar for peace (1946–47).

events.source: NCERT Class 8 Our Pasts III, Ch. 8 "The Making of the National Movement: 1870s–1947"

events.title: Interim Government
events.summary: An Interim Government under Jawaharlal Nehru takes office on 2 September 1946; the League joins in October.
events.detail: Nehru was Vice-President of the Viceroy's Executive Council (in effect Prime Minister). Patel held Home, Rajendra Prasad Food and Agriculture, Rajaji Education. The League joined in October; Liaquat Ali Khan took Finance.
causes: The Cabinet Mission plan provided for an interim government.
outcomes: Deadlock between Congress and League ministers made partition more likely.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Attlee's announcement
events.summary: On 20 February 1947 Attlee announces that Britain will leave India by June 1948 and sends Mountbatten.
events.detail: With violence spreading and the government losing control, the Labour government fixed a deadline for the transfer of power.
causes: Spread of communal violence; weakened British authority after the war.
outcomes: Mountbatten advanced the date to 15 August 1947.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

events.title: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan)
events.summary: On 3 June 1947 Mountbatten announces that India will be partitioned into two dominions, India and Pakistan.
events.detail: Punjab and Bengal assemblies would vote on partition; Sindh, Baluchistan, the NWFP (referendum) and Sylhet (referendum) would choose. Princely states could join either dominion. The Congress and League accepted.
causes: Failure of the Cabinet Mission and spreading violence (NCERT).
outcomes: Indian Independence Act passed by the British Parliament (18 July 1947).
Independence advanced to 15 August 1947.
events.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
facts: 3 June 1947: Mountbatten Plan announced.
The Indian Independence Act received royal assent on 18 July 1947.

events.title: Telangana armed struggle begins
events.summary: Peasants of Telangana rise against the Nizam's rule and the deshmukhs (landlords), led by the Communists and the Andhra Mahasabha (1946–51) (NCERT).
events.detail:
The peasantry of the Telangana region was the worst victim of the Nizam's oppressive rule and rose against him; women joined in large numbers (NCERT). Peasants fought vetti (forced labour), illegal levies and the grabbing of land by deshmukhs and jagirdars.

The spark was the killing of Doddi Komarayya at Kadavendi on 4 July 1946 by the men of the Visnur deshmukh, whom the washerwoman Chakali Ilamma had resisted. Armed dalams soon freed about 3,000 villages, where gram rajyams redistributed some ten lakh acres of land. The Communists and the Hyderabad State Congress were in the forefront (NCERT). After Operation Polo (1948) the Indian army fought the Communist squads too, and the CPI withdrew the struggle on 21 October 1951.
causes: Vetti (forced labour) and illegal exactions by deshmukhs and jagirdars.
Oppressive rule of the Nizam (NCERT).
Land grabbing by landlords.
course: 4 July 1946: Doddi Komarayya shot at Kadavendi.
1947–48: razakar terror; peasants form armed dalams and gram rajyams.
September 1948: Operation Polo ends the Nizam's rule.
1948–51: army operations against the Communist squads.
21 October 1951: CPI calls off the struggle.
gains: About 3,000 villages freed for a time; land redistributed.
outcomes: Weakened the Nizam and the deshmukhs; vetti ended.
Led to tenancy and jagir abolition laws in Hyderabad State.
Communists entered elections in 1951–52 (NCERT).
facts: Women joined the movement in large numbers (NCERT).
The Communists and the Hyderabad Congress led the movement against the Nizam (NCERT).
Ravi Narayana Reddy wrote "Veera Telangana Anubhavalu Gnapakalu" (APPSC Group-II 2025 key).

pairs.left: First martyr of the Telangana struggle

alsoOn.text: The CPI withdraws the Telangana armed struggle (21 October 1951) and joins the elections.

events.yearHook: 4 July 1946 → 1951: five years of the Telangana struggle.

participants.role: Led the struggle for the Communist Party.
Fought the deshmukh for her land.
Ruler whose regime the peasants fought.

events.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 1 "Challenges of Nation Building"; Andhra Pradesh history (AP SCERT / Telugu Akademi syllabus)

events.title: Kashmir joins India; first war with Pakistan
events.summary: Pakistan-backed tribal raiders invade Kashmir (22 October 1947); Maharaja Hari Singh signs the Instrument of Accession (26 October) and Indian troops land at Srinagar (NCERT).
events.detail:
Before 1947 Jammu and Kashmir was a princely state ruled by Hari Singh, who did not want to join India or Pakistan. The popular movement under Sheikh Abdullah wanted to get rid of the Maharaja but was against joining Pakistan (NCERT).

In October 1947 Pakistan sent tribal infiltrators to capture Kashmir. The Maharaja asked India for help; India sent troops only after he signed the Instrument of Accession (NCERT). V.P. Menon flew to Jammu for the signature. The raiders were driven out of the Valley, but part of the state stayed under Pakistani control. India took the issue to the UN (1 January 1948); the UN resolution of 21 April 1948 recommended a three-step process (NCERT). A ceasefire came on 1 January 1949.
causes: Hari Singh's wish to stay independent (NCERT).
Pakistan's tribal invasion (October 1947) (NCERT).
course: 22 October 1947: raiders cross into Kashmir.
26 October: Instrument of Accession signed.
27 October: Indian troops airlifted to Srinagar.
1 January 1948: India takes the issue to the UN.
21 April 1948: UN resolution (NCERT).
1 January 1949: ceasefire.
outcomes: J&K joined India; part of the state remained under Pakistan (NCERT).
Article 370 later gave the state special status (NCERT).
Kashmir became a lasting India–Pakistan dispute (NCERT).

treaties.name: Instrument of Accession (J&K)
terms: Defence, external affairs and communications handed to India.

alsoOn.text: UN resolution on Kashmir (21 April 1948); Sheikh Abdullah becomes PM of J&K (March 1948) (NCERT).

participants.role: Popular leader; became PM of J&K (March 1948) (NCERT).
PM who sent troops and took the issue to the UN.

events.source: NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, Ch. 7 "Regional Aspirations"

events.title: Kakinada Congress session and the Hindustani Seva Dal
events.summary: The 38th session of the Indian National Congress meets at Kakinada (Cocanada) in December 1923 under Maulana Mohammad Ali. Dr N. S. Hardikar founds the Hindustani Seva Dal, the Congress volunteer corps, at the same time.
events.detail:
This was the first all-India Congress session held in the Telugu districts. Debates were between the **Swarajists** (C. R. Das, Motilal Nehru, who wanted to enter councils) and the **No-changers** (who followed Gandhi's constructive work). The session let the Swarajists contest elections.

**Duvvuri Subbamma** organised women volunteers; **Konda Venkatappayya**, **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** and **Bulusu Sambamurti** were the local hosts.
events.source: Sarojini Regani, Highlights of the Freedom Movement in Andhra Pradesh; Telugu Akademi, Andhra Pradesh History; APPSC topic notes
events.yearHook: December 1923: one year after Chauri Chaura (1922) ended Non-Cooperation.
events.before: Non-Cooperation had been strong in Andhra (Chirala-Perala, Pedanandipadu, Palnadu, 1921–22) until Gandhi called it off.
events.after: The **Hindustani Seva Dal** trained volunteers for later satyagrahas (renamed Congress Seva Dal). Andhra next rose in the **Salt Satyagraha** (1930).
events.today: The Congress Seva Dal still traces its start to Kakinada, 1923.

events.title: Salt Satyagraha in Andhra
events.summary: When Gandhi breaks the salt law at Dandi (6 April 1930), Andhra volunteers make salt at many coastal places: Kakinada, Mattapalem, Vadarevu, Machilipatnam (Masulipatnam) and others.
events.detail:
Leaders and places: **Bulusu Sambamurti** — Kakinada; **Dandu Narayana Raju** — Mattapalem; **Kasi Viswanadham** — Vadarevu; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** — Masulipatnam. **Tanguturi Prakasam** led a salt camp at Madras. Women like **Durgabai** (Duvvuri Subbamma's co-worker) and **Unnava Lakshmi Bayamma** joined.

The song "**Veera gandhamu techinaramu, veerulevvaro telpudi**" (we have brought the hero's sandal paste — tell us who the heroes are) was sung to welcome volunteers.
events.source: Sarojini Regani, Highlights of the Freedom Movement in Andhra Pradesh; Telugu Akademi, Andhra Pradesh History; APPSC topic notes
events.yearHook: April 1930: the same days as Dandi (6 April 1930).
events.before: The **Simon Commission** boycott (1928) had made **Prakasam** a hero; the Congress declared **Purna Swaraj** at Lahore (1929).
events.after: Thousands were jailed; the movement ended with the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** (1931). In 1937 Congress ministries took office in Madras under **Rajagopalachari**, with Andhra ministers like Prakasam (revenue).
events.today: Kakinada's Bulusu Sambamurti is honoured by a statue; the salt pans of the Andhra coast still produce salt.
events.mnemonic: Andhra salt places "K-M-V-M": Kakinada (Bulusu), Mattapalem (Dandu Narayana Raju), Vadarevu (Kasi Viswanadham), Masulipatnam (Pattabhi).

examAngle.point: Salt Satyagraha in Andhra (1930): Bulusu Sambamurty at Kakinada, Dandu Narayana Raju at Mattapalem, Kasi Viswanadham at Vadarevu, Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Masulipatnam. The song "Veera gandhamu techinaramu" was sung then.
examAngle.context: Pair the person with the place; Kakinada and Masulipatnam were the two big centres because both towns had strong Congress groups and salt pans close by.

events.title: Quit India in Andhra: Tenali and Bhimavaram
events.summary: After the Congress leaders are arrested (9 August 1942), crowds in Andhra attack symbols of British rule. At Tenali (12 August) the railway station is burnt and police fire kills seven; at Bhimavaram the police station and other offices are attacked.
events.detail:
The **Andhra Circular**, issued by the Andhra Congress leaders, listed steps such as cutting telegraph lines and stopping trains — the British used it to blame the Congress for violence.

Other centres: **Chirala**, **Guntur**, **Kalipatnam**, **Kakinada** and student strikes at **Andhra University**. Many leaders (Prakasam, Pattabhi) were jailed until 1944–45.
events.source: Sarojini Regani, Highlights of the Freedom Movement in Andhra Pradesh; Telugu Akademi, Andhra Pradesh History; APPSC topic notes
events.yearHook: 12 August 1942: three days after the Quit India call (8–9 August 1942).
events.before: Andhra had joined the **individual satyagraha** (1940); the **Cripps Mission** (March 1942) failed.
events.after: After the war came the elections (1946); the **Telangana armed struggle** began in the Nizam's state (1946). India became free in **1947**; the demand for Andhra State came back at once.
events.today: A memorial to the Tenali martyrs of 1942 stands in the town.
